source_notes.cisco_ios: Conditions and remediation follow the CIS Cisco IOS Benchmark. Clause numbers are given for traceability and should be re-confirmed against your licensed copy of the benchmark for the exact IOS train you audit; rules whose clause could not be pinned exactly carry a section-level control_ref and a note.
source_notes.juniper_junos: The conditions in this pack are identical to those in the Cisco IOS pack, because both read the same vendor-neutral baseline fields - that is the point of the baseline. What is Junos-specific is the remediation, which is Junos CLI. Clause numbers are deliberately NOT asserted: the control intent below follows the CIS Juniper OS Benchmark, but the exact clause numbering could not be verified against a licensed copy, and inventing one would be worse than omitting it. Map each rule to its clause from your own copy before citing this output in a formal audit.
source_notes.fortinet_fortios: Clause numbers verified from CIS_Fortigate_7.0.x_Benchmark_v1.4.0.pdf (SHA256: 1692d30903ede16bd849aec848659520582b3d3154fd7e67de1794520b5f161b). For the full 56-recommendation CIS assessment, use the evaluate_cis_fortigate() pipeline which loads all rules from the knowledge base with PDF provenance.
source_notes.arista_eos: The conditions read the same vendor-neutral baseline fields as every other vendor pack. What is EOS-specific is the remediation, which is Arista EOS CLI. Clause numbers are deliberately NOT asserted: the control intent follows the CIS benchmark, but the exact clause numbering could not be verified against a licensed copy, and inventing one would be worse than omitting it.
source_notes.sonic_sonic: The conditions read the same vendor-neutral baseline fields as every other vendor pack. What is SONiC-specific is the remediation, which is SONiC CLI or Linux-level configuration. Clause numbers are deliberately NOT asserted.
source_notes.huawei_vrp: The conditions read the same vendor-neutral baseline fields as every other vendor pack. What is VRP-specific is the remediation, which is Huawei VRP CLI. Clause numbers are deliberately NOT asserted.
source_notes.checkpoint_gaia: The conditions read the same vendor-neutral baseline fields as every other vendor pack. What is Gaia-specific is the remediation, which is Check Point Gaia clish CLI. Clause numbers are deliberately NOT asserted.
source_notes.mikrotik_routeros: There is no official CIS benchmark for MikroTik RouterOS. The conditions mapped here are generic security best practices derived from other device benchmarks (e.g. Cisco IOS) to provide baseline security assessment for RouterOS. What is RouterOS-specific is the remediation CLI.
source_notes.sonicwall: There is no official CIS benchmark for SonicWall SonicOS. The conditions mapped here are generic security best practices derived from SonicWall official hardening guides (KB kA1VN0000000IRi0AM) and Tenable TNS Best Practices SonicWALL v5.9. What is SonicOS-specific is the remediation CLI.
source_notes.stormshield_sns: There is no official CIS benchmark for Stormshield Network Security. The conditions mapped here are generic security best practices derived from Stormshield official hardening guides and ANSSI recommendations. What is Stormshield-specific is the remediation CLI.
source_notes.watchguard_fireware: There is no official CIS benchmark for WatchGuard Firebox / Fireware. The conditions mapped here are generic security best practices derived from WatchGuard official hardening guides and security documentation. What is WatchGuard-specific is the remediation CLI and Web UI procedures.

fortinet_fortios.note: No direct CIS FortiGate clause maps to centralized AAA; closest is admin profile assignment (2.4.3)

sonicwall.note: No official CIS benchmark for SonicWall. Generic best-practice mapping from SonicWall hardening guide.
No official CIS benchmark for SonicWall. SonicOS does not support telnet; HTTP is the cleartext concern.

fortinet_fortios.note: FortiOS hashes admin passwords by default; CIS 2.4.1 checks the default admin password is changed

sonicwall.note: SonicOS stores admin passwords hashed by default.

fortinet_fortios.note: CIS 2.4.5 covers disabling HTTP admin access as part of encrypted-only channels
CIS FortiGate benchmark does not have a specific SSH v2 recommendation; FortiOS 7.x defaults to SSHv2

sonicwall.note: SonicOS SSH is always protocol version 2.

fortinet_fortios.note: CIS 2.3.1 covers SNMPv3-only which implicitly prevents v1/v2c write communities
